tradition.name: Indie Cristão
tradition.lineage: Indie Cristão connects Brazilian alternative Christian songwriters through independent recordings, collaborations and church-adjacent music communities. Artists such as Paulo Nazareth, Marcos Almeida and Os Arrais explore faith alongside everyday experience and poetic storytelling.

extras.description: Intimate voices and acoustic guitar support melodic, lyrically focused songs. Indie-pop and Brazilian influences also bring fuller band textures, contrasting arrangements and approaches that extend beyond congregational worship.

entries.geo_rationale: Artist own Spotify biography explicitly identifies Niterói origin; editorial artist-origin anchor, not claimed programme recording location.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Indie Cristão is the Brazilian alternative Christian songwriter community positively described in Eli Abraham’s firsthand interview: indie/Brazilian influences and a network naming Paulo Nazareth/Crombie, Marcos Almeida/Palavrantiga, Os Arrais and Estevão Queiroga, with poetic everyday-life expression that need not use explicit devotional vocabulary. Creator playlist includes Paulo’s Não É Mais Segredo at3 and Eli at19, confirming the named field rather than inferring classification from an acoustic arrangement. Existing christian_indie is a broad overlapping independent Christian umbrella, not confined to its Thief to King example; this is a narrower Brazilian interconnected songwriter scene, not a lexical replacement or claim of exclusion. Existing mpb_gospel overlaps Brazilian acoustic devotional song and already uses a voice-and-guitar branch; the difference is this evidenced alternative-songwriter network, not instrumentation. Existing brazilian_gospel covers the commercial evangelical recording sector; this community can participate in churches and that sector while also pursuing non-congregational poetic song. Existing brazilian_ccm includes a contemporary Catholic recording-community branch without asserting all CCM is Catholic; the present scene is not defined solely by denomination. Broad Brazilian indie and Christian folk fields can overlap these artists; no assertion of mutually exclusive membership is made.

tradition.name: Indie Liguria
tradition.lineage: Indie Liguria links independent music communities in Liguria, including Genoa’s bands, producers and small-label networks. Songwriting, electronic production and cross-cultural collaborations coexist within this regional scene.

tradition.name: Indie Nica
tradition.lineage: Indie Nica is Nicaragua’s independent music community, including self-managed songwriters, bands and production networks. Artists work across acoustic song, alternative music and other contemporary styles, both locally and in diaspora.

extras.description: Personal songwriting and melodic singing can be carried by piano or guitar, while band and electronic settings broaden the sound. Literary expression and spoken poetry also intersect with the scene.

entries.geo_rationale: Artist-owned profile positively identifies Managua/Nicaragua. Community origin anchor; actual selected recording is credited CostaRica and masteringGuatemala, neither silently relocated toManagua.

sources.support_notes: Fresh full13103view0 all5poems and complete sole text/voice/piano credits, CostaRica2020 home recording and separate Guatemala mix. Artist explicitly spoken-word poetry.
Fresh13103view2 full exactcreator field; CeshiaUbau19 with Marzo2020, a different work; ElBosque2. No claim selectedEP appears in playlist.
Fresh13103view1/13104view0 firsthand artist account explicitly independent self-managed/no label practice. LaterLuz arrangements not imported.

Fresh full13106view0 creator-owned ElBosque podcast, episode1 IndieNicaragua and regional independent artist/production community. Podcast is classification corroboration, not selected audio rendition.
Fresh13701view1 firsthand self-managed singer-songwriter work and piano training support general song branch instead of exact five-poem recital.

entries.neighbor_distinction: Indie Nica is the Nicaraguan independent-music community across styles, including diaspora practice. Exact creator roster names CeshiaUbau at19 and ElBosqueDeLosBuhos at2. Ubau describes her self-managed artist practice without a record label in a firsthand interview; the latter artist publishes the IndieNicaragua podcast and a regional independent-production support platform. This provides a positively named community beyond an isolated birthplace claim. Full old rock_nica is the broad national rock field, not only its Rexurgir hardcore exemplar; these fields substantially overlap, but the independent-community corpus also positively includes this self-issued poetry/piano branch and singer-songwriters. NuevaCancion is the historical political-song movement, not all current independent production, and spoken_word_poetry is a global medium rather than this national community. Selected EP is a documented literary offshoot of a positively included artist, not a claim every IndieNica work is spoken poetry or that all Nicaraguan artists are independent.

Broad functionalSong denotes an authored functional-harmonic verse/refrain/bridge treatment, not every experimental work. tradition.name: Japanese Buddhist chant
tradition.lineage: Japanese Buddhist chant encompasses the vocal practices of Japan’s Buddhist schools and lay communities. Transmitted from continental Asia and developed through distinct temple lineages, it ranges from elaborate shōmyō to syllabic sutra recitation, ceremonial narratives and devotional hymns. Clergy and lay practitioners preserve these traditions through ritual, instruction and communal singing.

extras.description: Voices carry sacred texts through sustained melodic phrases or measured syllabic recitation. Some rituals use bells, bowls, gongs and cymbals as signals, while vocal passages place the sound and meaning of the text at the centre of the practice.
exemplars: Shōmyō, sutra recitation, kōshiki and goeika traditions

tradition.name: Japanese VGM
tradition.lineage: Japanese VGM develops through Japan’s game-production studios, composers and music audiences, from constrained early hardware to streamed and orchestral scores. Concerts, recordings and adaptations carry game themes into listening cultures beyond play.

extras.description: Recurring themes, looping patterns and changing instrumental layers connect melody with game worlds and action. Synthesized timbres, piano and orchestral colors span intimate cues, energetic sequences and dramatic scores, with arrangements adapting to both hardware and narrative needs.

entries.geo_rationale: The Tenth Mosaic official2026 game-culture event at Institut francais du Japon Tokyo presents Japanese game-music composers and performances. Tokyo is an editorial field-community anchor, not the location of this sheet edition or a claimed Uematsu session.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Japanese VGM denotes the Japanese game-music production, circulation and adaptation field, not an ethnicity test or a claim every creator is resident in Japan. Original research by Lehtonen documents a historically specific Japanese media/author/composer institution that promoted game cues into a public genre beyond in-game use; Merlini independently studies its cross-style compositional culture. Exact creator field includes Uematsu and Japanese game sound teams alongside international adapters and Chinese game composers. Existing video_game_music already includes Japanese console history and later orchestral delivery; it remains a broader global umbrella, not an exclusively Western or chip-only field. Existing vgm_instrumental and vgm_remix, plus lo_fi_vgm and queued rhythm_game, overlap through performance, reworking, treatment or game-mechanic axes; none is silently reduced to one exemplar. This regional-industrial repertoire field crosses those axes and includes original score as well as worldwide reinterpretations. Current piano edition is only a bounded representative, not the category-defining distinction. Japanese soundtrack/anison/KoreanSoundtrack fields concern adjacent screen/repertoire communities and may share composers; game music is not presumed synonymous with animation music.

extras.description: Voices and guitar-led songs meet bass, keyboards, drums and hand percussion. Melodic phrasing, rhythmic contrast and layered accompaniment create a flexible sound that retains Kabyle expression while drawing on varied musical influences.

tradition.name: Korean Soundtrack
tradition.lineage: Korean soundtrack music brings original songs and dramatic scores together across film and television production. Composers, singers and studio musicians shape themes that connect characters, settings and emotion, with recordings and arrangements extending their life beyond the screen.

extras.description: Expressive vocal melodies, piano, guitar and string textures support themes and transitions. Electronic production and acoustic performance coexist, ranging from intimate song settings to expansive dramatic writing.

tradition.name: Lagu Iban
tradition.lineage: Lagu Iban encompasses Iban-language songs and recording communities in Sarawak and their wider circulation. Artists such as Masterpiece connect local language and identity with contemporary rock, pop and other popular forms.

extras.description: Sung melodies and recurring refrains meet guitar, keyboards, bass and drums. Contrasting lead and backing voices, instrumental responses and changing band textures support songs about relationships, experience and community.

The artist explicitly discusses the Iban/Dayak music industry, its local labels, audiences and distribution in a firsthand interview; this is positive community evidence, not birthplace alone. Exact creator playlist includes Masterpiece at positions51 and62 among a much broader Iban-language artist field. Existing malaysian_pop and classic_malaysian_pop already cover broad popular recording histories; their full scopes are acknowledged, not reduced to exemplars. The narrower Iban linguistic recording community differs from Malay-language mainstream pop without asserting that national fields exclude Iban artists. Existing malaysian_indie, malaysian_traditional and borneo_traditional also overlap geography and heritage: the first is an independent-production scene, the latter two broad traditional-repertoire fields, neither synonymous with the entire Iban-language contemporary recording network. This rock band is one complete branch, not a universal Iban ensemble or an equation between Iban and all Dayak peoples.

tradition.name: Lagu Tarling
tradition.lineage: Lagu Tarling belongs to the song traditions of Cirebon and Indramayu on Java’s north coast. Earlier guitar-and-flute music developed into varied popular-song and dramatic forms, with modern branches incorporating dangdut influences and electronic keyboards.

extras.description: Singing carries the regional repertoire over melodic accompaniment and repeating percussion patterns. Guitar and flute remain part of its historical sound; modern organ-tunggal performances use an arranger keyboard to combine those timbres with bass, chords and rhythmic backing.
exemplars: Modern Indramayu Organ Tunggal Tarling — documented singer/arranger-keyboard practice, Rasriy and Wahyudin 2023

tradition.lineage: Mapouka — Ivorian coastal dance and its lively youssoumba vocal-percussion accompaniment.

extras.description: Mapouka is an Ivorian coastal dance associated with lively youssoumba accompaniment. Lead singing, harmonized responses, drumming and rhythmic bottle playing support its energetic movement; some performers also add spoken toasting. Groups such as Aboutou Roots and Nigui Saff K-Dance helped bring village-rooted practice to commercial recordings and wider stages.

tradition.name: Middle Eastern Traditional
tradition.lineage: Middle Eastern traditional music encompasses interconnected Arab, Turkish, Persian, Armenian and neighboring regional repertoires, from modal instrumental improvisation to vocal art music and communal songs.

extras.description: Modal melodies, ornamented phrases and exchanges between composed repertoire and improvisation connect many of these traditions, while their tuning systems, rhythms and forms remain regionally distinct. Oud, bowed strings, qanun, nay and percussion appear in varied ensembles; instrumental solos and singing provide contrasting settings. The Iraqi oud tradition offers one intimate expression of this wider musical world.
exemplars: William & Mary Middle Eastern Music Ensemble

entries.model_policy: Genre-level representative Iraqi solo-oud branch. Ornamented melodic plucking, eleven strings, plastic risha, walnut ribs, spruce face and modern nylon set are a coherent authored conventional oud realization, not a measured AlHaj instrument. Iraqi school is positively justified by the selected traditional-practice source. Wider voices/ensembles described publicly are not imposed as an obligatory union or claimed absent. Global temperament omitted because regional modal tuning cannot honestly be reduced to universal twelve-tone equal temperament. Studio and chain are authored listening choices.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Full arab_folk is a broad Arab folk field, not merely its Bahariya guitar/oud example; this larger regional umbrella also positively includes non-Arab Persian, Turkish, Armenian and Greek traditions. Full arabic_instrumental includes Arabic instrumental practice beyond its selected taqsim, while this field includes vocal repertoire and non-Arab traditions. oud_taqsim, iraqi_maqam and arab_tarab are specific instrumental or vocal modal practices contained within/overlapping the wider field. The representative Iraqi oud rendering need not stand outside these narrower fields to represent a separately evidenced broader umbrella; no claim of disjointness or different mechanism.

tradition.name: Moorish Traditional
tradition.lineage: Moorish traditional music carries the azawan heritage of Mauritania’s hereditary iggawin musicians. Its codified modal practice encompasses praise, love songs and dance, with contemporary performances also incorporating electric instruments.

extras.description: Voices interact with the rippling strings of the ardin and the plucked tidinit, supported by tbal drumming. Electric guitar can extend the melodic accompaniment. Modal development and exchanges between singing and instruments shape a varied professional repertoire.
exemplars: Dimi Mint Abba and Khalifa Ould Eide — Moorish Music from Mauritania (1990)

entries.neighbor_distinction: Moorish Traditional is the ethnocultural hereditary azawan/iggawin heritage field within, and overlapping, the broader national musique_mauritanienne category. The full existing national entry explicitly includes a Moorish electric branch and is not defined solely by its Noura exemplar. Philharmonie ethnomusicologist Michel Guignard distinguishes Mauritania’s Moorish, Pulaar, Soninke and Wolof patrimonies and identifies the Moorish professional lineage; this positive ethnocultural scope, not a different artist/date, supports the narrower category. Exact creator playlist7khkEkukvAQWdDapKh1lVt includes this Dimi/Khalifa pairing. Full existing sahel_praise explicitly includes Mauritania and contemporary regional praise recordings, so there is genuine overlap in praise-function material. Moorish azawan heritage also encompasses love, dance and codified modal repertoire, broader in function but narrower ethnoculturally than that transregional praise field. Existing Mande kora/jeli categories overlap professional praise practices but do not define all Moorish modal heritage. This category can include modern electric realizations of inherited repertoire, without claiming an acoustic-only or premodern boundary.
entries.model_policy: Broad artMusic is scoped to the positively codified azawan modal system and hereditary specialist transmission documented by the Philharmonie; no Western notation, concert-only function or universal through-composition is inferred. Authored acoustic concert-hall listening realization retains every credited role. All human vocal controls are retained with source-unspecified physiology, training, ornament and pitch; count/tracking remain unknown. Source confirms singing but detailed word-setting remains unspecified. Existing large-calabash ardin with rippling accompaniment and traditional tidinit with grave modal-way coloring are authored representative choices, not a claim all album tracks use one mode. Electric guitar uses an explicitly authored alder/maple single-coil, clean arpeggiated modal accompaniment technique and standard tuning, without measured original gear or temperament claims. The tbal uses museum-documented hollow wooden hemispherical shell, cowhide head and bare-hand metric variation; exact diameter, wood species, tension attachment and original player remain unspecified. No extra vocalist or instrument is inferred from institutional practice descriptions.

tradition.name: Música Aguascalentense
tradition.lineage: Música Aguascalentense brings together the regional music communities of Aguascalientes, from northern and tropical dance styles to independent rock and hybrid ensembles. Local festivals and musicians such as La Santísima Voladora connect regional identity with wider Mexican popular music.

extras.description: Driving guitar and bass, drums, percussion, brass responses and keyboards meet expressive singing in the region’s rock–tropical fusion. Other branches draw on mariachi, norteño and cumbia traditions.

entries.geo_rationale: Producer address and named regional formation/circulation; not the Madrid institutional presentation site.

entries.neighbor_distinction: Música Aguascalentense is a regional circulation field crossing cumbia, norteño, mariachi and hybrid rock/tropical practices, not an equivalence to one national style. The Instituto Cultural de Aguascalientes independently publishes a crossstyle local festival field. Existing latin_rock already includes broad Latin American rhythmic rock beyond Santana, and mexican_indie includes national independent bands beyond Sadfields; both can overlap this regional subset. Existing mexican_pop defines the balada recording industry, while full cumbia_sonidera describes a sound-system/dedication practice and its studio extensions. None is an alternative name for this regional network. Do not universalize the selected metal/cumbia hybrid across all regional music.

tradition.name: Música Coahuilense
tradition.lineage: Música Coahuilense connects regional repertoires and popular-music communities across Coahuila. Northern dance traditions, tropical bands and contemporary ensembles circulate through local celebrations, recording networks and migration.

extras.description: Singing, rhythmic bass and drums meet guitar, keyboards and melodic wind responses in tropical dance settings. Cumbia grooves and northern regional styles offer contrasting approaches within this wider musical landscape.

entries.geo_rationale: All six performers explicitly identified as from Nueva Rosita; editorial regional-community anchor, not a claimed recording studio.
entries.neighbor_distinction: The creator category expressly spans Coahuila regional popular-music groups: Massore, Tropicalisimo Apache, Chicos de Barrio and northern conjuntos from Acuna, Sabinas and Nueva Rosita. This is not a birthplace-only invention: the federal cultural funding register independently names Musica coahuilense de antano con jovenes and Difusion de la musica nortena de compositores coahuilenses as regional repertoire projects. Those projects substantiate regional cultural organization, not participation by Massore. Existing cumbia_lagunera is the full Comarca Lagunera cumbia scene including Apache/Chicos de Barrio, not merely its electronic Cumbia Xillers exemplar; Coahuilense overlaps that scene but also includes Coahuila northern-border conjunto and Nueva Rosita repertoire outside that subregion. Existing norteno explicitly includes Coahuila and remains overlapping, while its accordion/bajo-sexto lineage is not the entire regional field. Existing grupera and tropical encompass this selected tropical dance branch; musica_mexicana remains a broad modern national umbrella. Neither different personnel nor source saxophone supplies the category boundary.

tradition.name: Música michoacana
tradition.lineage: Música michoacana encompasses the musical communities of Michoacán, including Purépecha song, arpa-grande and valona traditions, and regional brass bands. State archives and local performers preserve a broad repertoire across the state’s regions and generations.

extras.description: Guitar-accompanied singing forms one intimate strand of this regional music. Interlocking voices and plucked chordal accompaniment carry lyrical songs, alongside the larger harp ensembles, choirs and wind bands heard elsewhere in the field.

entries.neighbor_distinction: Read the full existing musica_purepecha and tierra_caliente records, not only their exemplars. The selected duo directly overlaps Purépecha pirekua; it is not evidence of a newly distinct pirekua technique. The named state-wide field is broader: the exact creator playlist includes Purépecha song and chorus (Grupo Erandi, Dueto Masculino, Coro Tarasco Zezangari), arpa-grande/valona ensembles and multiple regional brass bands. The state archive independently defines its regional remit across styles, geographies and generations and explicitly includes this state-affiliated duo. This supports the regional umbrella beyond the indigenous Purépecha and Balsas Tierra Caliente fields, while acknowledging substantial overlap. No exact creator membership for Sïrankua is asserted. National Mexican music and neighboring state labels do not replace this specifically documented community. No coextensive Michoacán umbrella appears among current old or accepted queued entries. functionalSong.mexican represents the expressly authored strophic tonal rendition, not every music in the state.
entries.model_policy: Authored two-singer, two-guitar rendition with recurring strophes and tonal chord support for the selected lyrical song practice. Both credited guitars share the classical-guitar card; spruce tops, Torres fan bracing, high-tension nylon strings, standard tuning, fingerpicking and rest-stroke attack are explicit coherent editorial construction and gesture choices, not measured source models or string materials. historical_source_audits.classification_evidence: Música Nayarita names a regional musical community spanning Nayarit and its migrant fair network, not a single instrumental style. Creator repertoire includes Banda Móvil, Banda R15, Cohuich, Torbellinos and Invierno Musical, with brass bandas and electrified dance groups; selected Hechizeros membership in that exact playlist is not claimed. Existing tecnobanda already includes several shared creator artists and this selected electronic-tecnobanda branch overlaps it. The distinction is the positively documented regional and diaspora institution, broader than that specific style, not a new ensemble alone. extras.description: Timor-Leste’s popular music connects Tetun and other local song traditions with Portuguese, Indonesian and international pop influences. Guitar-led bands, keyboards, bass and drums have supported social dancing and public song since the late colonial period. Music also carries memories of displacement and national identity, alongside everyday entertainment.

tradition.lineage: Música triste brasileira links Brazilian internet-era sad-pop and rap audiences through vulnerable songwriting and collaborative digital circulation.

extras.description: Melancholic lead vocals sit over acoustic guitar and keyboard support in the pop-oriented branch. Connected phrases and reflective lyrics foreground personal emotion; Hiosaki exemplifies this strand without defining all Brazilian melancholy as one style.

entries.neighbor_distinction: The creator Música Triste Brasileira playlist includes Hiosaki at item8 alongside Tuono, Zant, VMZ and Sadstation. His firsthand interview describes a youth internet audience and his own melancholic-pop practice evolving from indie/lofi, with personal sadness and vulnerability. This records the Brazilian Portuguese-language sad-pop/rap audience and collaborative discovery field, not every historically melancholy MPB song. Existing sad_rap_emo_trap and emo_rap describe the wider US/internet trap-and-guitar rap lineage; overlap with those fields is explicit, while the selected pop song and Brazilian youth community are not universally trap. Existing sadcore is the American indie songwriting lineage; trap_triste describes Spanish-language Latin-trap grammar. Existing Brazilian popular and hip-hop fields overlap more broadly, rather than being excluded. A different Hiosaki song or acoustic instrumentation alone is not the category distinction. Existing brazilian_emo is a national indie/emo band field and its Baztian trio is only an exemplar; Brazilian sad-pop/rap overlaps emotional themes but the positively identified internet pop/rap audience and cross-style discovery roster are not defined by an emo-rock band lineage.

tradition.name: Musique traditionnelle congolaise
tradition.lineage: Congolese traditional music encompasses the country’s diverse regional and cultural repertoires, from lamellophone-accompanied song to choral, ritual and dance traditions. Contemporary ensembles also reinterpret inherited material with amplified instruments.

extras.description: Voices and interlocking instrumental patterns shape varied local practices. In an intimate song strand, a singer accompanies personal verses on the lukembi, alternating vocal phrases with resonant plucked-metal-key figures; larger ensembles and communal vocal traditions supply other textures.

tradition.name: New Hampshire indie
tradition.lineage: New Hampshire indie connects independent artists, venues and festivals across the state, including communities around Peterborough and Keene. Acoustic songwriting, indie rock and pop-punk coexist within these local networks.

tradition.name: Oeteldonk
tradition.lineage: Oeteldonk music belongs to the carnival culture of ’s-Hertogenbosch, sustained by local clubs, song competitions and community celebrations. New carnival songs join familiar refrains in the Kwèkfestijn and a shared repertoire associated with the city’s festive identity.

extras.description: Projecting voices, memorable refrains and lively wind-band responses invite collective participation. Trumpets, trombones, saxophones and low brass combine with rhythmic percussion, while humorous texts and theatrical presentation animate the songs.

entries.geo_rationale: Oeteldonk is the official carnival community of Den Bosch; geographic anchor names its city, not a measured recording location.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Oeteldonk is the positively documented Den Bosch carnival repertoire community: its own institution describes150–200clubs, annual original-song Kwèkfestijn competition with60-plus entrants and eleven issued finalists, plus a separate accompanied children festival. Exact creator map includes Wim Kersten, De Twee Pinten, Van Alles Wè and many named local carnival clubs. The arranger explicitly tags this medley Oeteldonk, connecting the edition to the institutional repertoire rather than merely a Dutch place of birth. Existing dweilorkest already covers Dutch festive wind/percussion bands across carnival and other events, without fixed instrumentation; Oeteldonk overlaps that ensemble practice but names a specific songwriting/festival/repertoire network that also includes singers and children performances. Existing dutch_pop/classic_dutch_pop cover broad national popular-music histories, and levenslied the sentimental song tradition; these remain inclusive overlapping umbrellas rather than categories limited to their current exemplars. Accepted carnaval_limburg is a different positively documented regional carnival network, not all Dutch carnival. British brass-band contest practice is not an alias: this edition retains saxophones and Dutch carnival repertoire. The issued wind-only arrangement is a representative branch, not the proposed category boundary by itself.

tradition.name: Oldschool Deutschrap
tradition.lineage: Oldschool Deutschrap gathers the foundational generations of German-language hip hop, from the 1990s scenes of Heidelberg, Stuttgart, Hamburg and Munich to early-2000s street rap. Advanced Chemistry, Die Fantastischen Vier, Freundeskreis, Absolute Beginner and Fettes Brot helped shape its varied approaches to language, identity and everyday life.

extras.description: Rhythmic verses, boom-bap grooves, sampled phrases and DJ scratching characterize much of the repertoire. Humour, social commentary and street narratives coexist across regional scenes and remain influential in later German rap.

classification_evidence.note: Oldschool Deutschrap is the retrospectively curated historical German-language hip-hop cohort, positively organized as a distinct broadcaster programming field by bigFM across Munich, Heidelberg, Stuttgart, Hamburg and Berlin. Its definition includes1990s pioneers and early2000s street-rap successors, so it is not reduced to pre1992 or to boom-bap alone. Apple Music editorial identifies Fettes Brot’s1995/1996 hits as an established oldschool canon. Existing german_deutschrap is the full historical-to-current German-language umbrella, explicitly including those pioneers and later trap/drill streaming generations: the new field overlaps as a historical-cohort subset rather than claiming the old row omitted its roots. Hamburg hip-hop is locality rather than this cross-city retrospective community. This2013 separately issued rendition by a canonical historical act is a selected continuing practice of that cohort, not a claim that2013 was the birth era or that every later release by an older performer belongs to a distinct sonic style. The source’s lack of accompaniment does not define the category.

tradition.name: Otacore
tradition.lineage: Otacore connects fan-made songs and remixes inspired by games, cartoons and other screen worlds. Newgrounds, YouTube and related fandom networks helped artists circulate character narratives and original pop songs across national and stylistic boundaries.

extras.description: Character-led singing meets keyboard melodies, synthesized bass and bright electronic figures, with arranged samples and vocoded color expanding the texture. Direct hooks and contrasting song sections support theatrical or emotionally expressive storytelling across a varied fan-music field.

entries.geo_rationale: Arranger platform own biography identifies Andrew Wrangell and Samuel Dickenson as Brisbane musicians. Editorial selected-edition production-community anchor; not origin or exclusive location of the global fandom category, and not a claim of the source recording room.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Otacore is treated as the named transnational fan-created-media-song discovery community, not a physical sound or synonym for all anime music. Exact creator corpus includes MLP-associated Frozen Night24 and 4everfreebrony26, Hazbin fan-song Insane87 and Addict38, FNAF works58/61/64/68/81/88, and Doki Doki Literature Club fan song90. Landau firsthand describes the wider internet practice of producing songs/remixes for fans of games, cartoons, films and shows; that community evidence is not a claim that The Living Tombstone appears in the currently returned first100. Selected Black Gryph0n/Baasik exact-song membership is separately positive. Full nerdcore and queued anime_rap are rap-specific geek/anime narrative fields and overlap without exhausting the cross-style fan-song corpus. Full geek_rock/geek_folk likewise overlap geek storytelling but are not all cross-media fandom production; no distinction rests on a different pianist. Anison and anison_anime_song are commissioned Japanese animation-title industries, while video_game_music concerns interactive scores and gaming_edm licensed gameplay background music. Fan-created character songs may later become licensed or involve voice actors; Otacore is not asserted wholly amateur, unofficial or disjoint from these industries. Existing anime_piano scopes arrangements of anime songs and does not exhaust Western game/cartoon fan works. Broad soundtrack/cartoon fields also overlap, but their original-production repertoire does not make all independent fan retellings identical.

entries.model_policy: Genre-level electronic fan-song production replaces a solo-piano transcription as universal default. Landau firsthand testimony describes loop arrangement, piano-roll keyboard writing, synth/bass design and vocoder-treated singing. Preserve voice, synthesizer, software sample arrangement, vocoder and piano roles. Author a six-operator harmonic polyphonic FM instrument with short envelopes as a representative melodic/bass sound-design option; DX7 lineage is a concrete authored alternative, not a claim that Sytrus/Harmor is a DX7. Modern upright is an authored piano-tone rendition of the positive keyboard role, not source acoustic hardware. Twenty-plus-band saw-carrier vocal processing is authored, not a measured VocodeX preset. No whole-master sampler or invented exact band roster. Prior licensed solo-piano edition remains archived; functional-harmonic verse/chorus/bridge form is the authored song realization.
entries.source_scope_limitation: Representative broader fan-song production; source digital tools do not establish this authored physical gear or exact controls. No claim to reconstruct the Insane master.

Publisher explicitly specifies instrumental solo, piano, no lyrics and moderate swing. One pianist and zero voices in this separately issued complete arrangement, not a reduction by the researcher of the original sung/electronic recording. Full paid notation and audio were not inspected; exact voicing, piano subtype and source performance details are unknown. The selected song is exact creator Otacore item87. Official artist-channel metadata calls it a Hazbin Hotel song; mirrored artist description explains its independent character-song creation and approval by the show creator. The mirror is explicitly attributed, not claimed freshly retrieved full YouTube description or proof it is an official soundtrack cue. Source-unspecified piano subtype is rendered as an authored standard studio upright with connected melodic legato phrasing, compatible with the published moderate-swing rhythm and not a claim that legato means straight rhythm or classical repertoire. Controlled live-room space is an editorial recording presentation. Broad functionalSong is an authored verse–chorus–bridge rendition organized over functional chord progressions, not a claim that the unseen six-page score follows every structural choice. All source composition material remains within the selected complete piano edition; no original vocalist, synthesizer or drums are discarded from a claimed full master. No global tuning, measured room, capture equipment or original keyboard implementation is invented.

tradition.name: Polish Alternative
tradition.lineage: Polish alternative music brings independent and experimental approaches into popular song, crossing guitar rock, alternative pop and electronic production. Its varied artists connect melodic songwriting with exploratory textures and arrangements.

extras.description: Singing, electric guitars, bass and drums form one band-oriented foundation, with synthesizers adding harmonic or textural colour. Some arrangements expand into organs, electric piano, processed voices and horns, while others foreground electronic production and sparse pop structures.

entries.geo_rationale: Artist-owned album profile names Szczecin,Poland; editorial artist locality, not a claimed recording address.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Polish Alternative is an overlapping cross-style national alternative-song field, broader than alternative rock alone. The artist explicitly self-tags this complete album Polish Alternative alongside alternative pop/rock. The exact creator field spans Natalia Przybysz, Rosalie., Coals, The Dumplings, Bass Astral x Igo and multiple other acts; no Lobotomia membership is falsely asserted. Adam Mickiewicz Institute cultural curation independently names a Polish alternative-pop scene and its synth-heavy Bokka branch, so the broader pop/electronic reach does not rest solely on a different saxophone arrangement. tradition.name: Polish Indie
tradition.lineage: Polish indie is a cross-style independent music network connecting artists, labels and audiences across Poland. Guitar-based rock, electronics, improvisation and folk-informed work share independent production and circulation rather than a single fixed sound.

extras.description: In its instrumental alternative-rock strand, clean guitar patterns, electric bass and drums combine with synthesizer colour. Interlocking rhythmic figures and changes in texture build momentum, with a direct ensemble sound emphasizing detail and contrast.

tradition.name: Portuguese Indie
tradition.lineage: Portugal’s independent-music networks connect local songwriting, self-directed production, labels and live venues across rock, pop, electronic music and other styles.

extras.description: Guitar-led songs, melodic singing and a bass-and-drum rhythm section form an established strand, often expanded by keyboards and electronic textures. Independent production and circulation connect these varied approaches, alongside continuing exchanges with the wider Portuguese popular-music field.

entries.geo_rationale: Editorial Lisbon-area source production anchor: label names São Domingos de Benfica additional recording/mixing and Dafundo initial recording; not a claim all takes occurred at the coordinate.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Portuguese indie denotes the national independent production, circulation and discovery community. Primary interview research by Ana Oliveira examines71 participants and treats independence as a continuum across genres rather than a fixed rock sound or absolute exclusion of mainstream commerce. The creator corpus includes Cassete Pirata, Capicua, Noiserv, Octa Push and other cross-style participants; RTP independently identifies Cassete Pirata with the Portuguese indie scene. Full existing portuguese_indie_rock is the overlapping rock branch (its Pega Monstro duo is a representative, not a category restriction); this broader independent community also encompasses electronic, hip-hop and intimate song practice. Existing portuguese_pop_modern covers mainstream national pop, portuguese_experimental experimental practice, and Lisbon/Madeira regional categories geographic fields. These overlap but do not replace the independent-community axis. Neither the selected four-person arrangement nor the date creates the boundary. No claim all community music is rock, unsigned or outside major-label distribution.

tradition.name: Puerto Rican indie
tradition.lineage: Puerto Rico’s independently organized recording and live-music communities connect alternative rock, pop, experimental music and locally rooted styles.

tradition.name: Raspe
tradition.lineage: Raspe is a Honduran dance-music current rooted in the north-coast scene. Producers and singers combine electronic melody with dancehall-derived percussion, developing a local name and community through songs, parties and online circulation.

extras.description: Electronic melodic hooks, low-frequency support and syncopated percussion frame rhythmic singing. Repeated phrases and changes in instrumental density give the tracks their dance focus, with influences from reggae, dancehall and contemporary electronic production.

entries.geo_rationale: Country-level repertoire-community anchor documented by primary producer interview and expressly named in selected mix; not DJ birthplace or source recording location (profile says Bronx).
entries.source_scope_limitation: Genre-practice evidence, no exact single-master reconstruction or claim every raspe track has one singer.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Raspe is a positively named Honduran north-coast dancehall/electronic dance current. First-person2025 interview with producer ALEMVN and Fresh Bodden explains melodic electronics plus dancehall percussion, a north-coast dance term and circulation through KBP and other precursors into national/diasporic venues. Exact creator roster corroborates KBP, ALEMVN, Jr Clark, Big Nango and associated collaborations; it is not evidence every DJ selection belongs exclusively to this roster. Actual musica_hondurena is broader national repertoire and its Candú score only an exemplar; this is a narrower contemporary dance-production community with overlap, not a nationality-only claim. Garifuna punta/punta-rock specifically retain historical drum/dance lineage, whereas this source names a distinct electronic/dancehall fusion; Jamaican dancehall and reggaeton are influential broader/adjacent practices, not synonyms. Queued regionally named Latin/Caribbean scenes do not erase this positively identified Honduran current. Selected Dj Andy is not claimed a mapped artist; his issuer explicitly identifies requested style.

tradition.name: Ritmo Kombina
tradition.lineage: Ritmo Kombiná developed in Curaçao in the early 1990s through Gibi Doran and collaborating dance-band musicians. It brings together rhythmic influences from soca and merengue with the bass and keyboard language of cadence and zouk.

extras.description: Singing rides over interlocking conga and drum-kit patterns, with bass and keyboards shaping the harmonic groove. Repeating figures, rhythmic accents and changes in arrangement keep the music directed toward dancing. Brass and timbales can expand the band sound, while local radio and diaspora audiences sustain the repertoire.

entries.geo_rationale: Editorial on-island Curaçao community anchor supported by issuer history, not DJ residence, recording venue or birthplace.
entries.source_scope_limitation: Primary research book retrieved through full indexed author upload; direct flipbook open failed. No audio audition or exact recording reconstruction claim. Earlier programme-only record preserved in full evidence.
entries.neighbor_distinction: The station first-person history documents a Curaçaoan and island-diaspora listener community cultivated through RadioFruz from2003, renamed Fruzitime in2011 and now Caribbeanvibe, with an explicit Ritmo Kombina mission and continuing DJs/programmes. This is a positively named contemporary dance-repertoire community, not all Caribbean music. Existing kompa is Haitian compas lineage, zouk the Guadeloupe/Martinique studio field, kaseko Surinamese Creole dance practice; influence and audience overlap do not make the institutional Curaçaoan field identical. Existing antilliaanse_folklore is broader Netherlands-Antillean folklore with Palm dance-piano selected branch; not restricted to that exemplar, but the contemporary named radio/dance community is an additional axis. No exact EveryNoise performer membership reproduced or claimed. The website genre-history paragraph attributed to Wikipedia is not used as primary historical proof.

tradition.name: Rumba (Spanish popular song)
tradition.lineage: Spanish popular rumba developed through intersecting Romani, Catalan and urban musical communities, drawing on Afro-Cuban rhythmic exchange and flamenco-related guitar practice. Peret, Los Chichos and the Gipsy Kings helped carry its danceable songs into wider popular circulation.

extras.description: Propulsive strummed guitar, expressive singing and recurring refrains drive the music. Hand percussion, bass and contemporary band arrangements can extend its rhythmic foundation, while guitar flourishes and vocal responses maintain a communal, celebratory character.

entries.geo_rationale: Artist-owned history identifies formation in Arles; editorial repertoire-artist anchor, not claimed score publication/recording place or exclusive rumba origin.
entries.neighbor_distinction: The immutable rumba label is interpreted through its actual creator corpus as the Spanish popular rumba and cross-border Gitano rumba field, not as an unqualified world umbrella merging Cuban and Congolese traditions. Display qualification makes this explicit. The creator includes Los Chunguitos, Los Chichos, Las Grecas, Peret and Gipsy Kings; Bamboleo itself appears at71. Instituto Cervantes programmes rumba across Peret/GatoPerez and LosChichos/LosChunguitos, extending to newer rock, rap, pop and techno mixtures. The artists own history specifically identifies Bamboleo with Rumba Gitano and Spanish Romani connections in southern France. Existing rumba_catalana positively covers the Barcelona Catalan Gitano tradition and overlaps Peret, its rhythms and descendants; it is not merely one exemplar, and the selected French Gitano branch shares Catalan ancestry. The broader institutional popular-rumba field also encompasses non-Barcelona Spanish branches and newer mixtures, rather than excluding Catalan rumba. Existing nuevo_flamenco covers a wider cross-style flamenco-fusion current, overlapping some artists but not synonymous with rumba repertoire and its community. Full Cuban rumba/yambu/columbia and Congolese/Lingala rumba records have different defined historical practices; their name overlap does not establish equivalence. A solo keyboard edition is one positively issued rendition of this repertoire, not the usual ensemble or a claim the whole field is instrumental.

tradition.lineage: Russian contemporary Christian music connects Russian-language churches, ministry networks and diasporic communities through devotional popular song. Recorded worship and family ensembles circulate across Russia, other post-Soviet countries and communities abroad.

extras.description: Melodic singing conveys prayer, praise and testimony through contemporary song forms. Piano-supported performances coexist with band arrangements and congregational singing, linking intimate devotion with collective worship.

tradition.name: Russian Hyperpop
tradition.lineage: Russian hyperpop developed through online youth music communities around the turn of the 2020s, combining pop songwriting with exaggerated electronic production and the circulation of short-form video. Sqwore, 17Seventeen, rizza, treepside and Midix form part of its varied scene.

extras.description: Strongly altered voices, synthetic bass, fragmented samples and abrupt shifts in texture give familiar pop gestures an unstable digital character. Singing and rap mingle with pitched vocal effects, glitches and dense electronic beats.
exemplars: Note-Store — Sqwore Пластиковые воспоминания, complete Piano.Easy PEA0334385

entries.geo_rationale: Approximate on-land country anchor for positively documented Russian scene, not source recording city, artist residence or arranger location.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Russian Hyperpop is a positively documented Russian youth/internet production and listening scene within the broad international hyperpop field. Antipova2026 original research examines a Russian corpus including Sqwore,17Seventeen,rizza,treepside and Midix, its online circulation and specific repertory; it directly analyzes the selected song on Eve. This is evidence of an actual regional scene, not a category inferred only from artist nationality. The paper’s broad psychological or political interpretations are not adopted as factual attributes of listeners. Full existing hyperpop already spans international internet/Discord/SoundCloud/TikTok maximalist pop; Russian Hyperpop overlaps it as a narrower scene, not an absent technical invention. Full hyperpop_rap preserves rap-led crossover rather than all sung/electronic hyperpop, and may overlap. Existing russian_pop, russian_alt_pop and russian_electronic remain broader national fields, not restricted to their selected Neriberry/OQJAV/Kedr examples. The exact creator map and playlist positively identify a Russian hyperpop corpus; selected Sqwore membership is supported by original research, not falsely claimed in the first100 playlist positions. The piano arrangement does not itself establish category distinctness.

tradition.name: Russian Indie
tradition.lineage: Russian indie develops through independent bands, labels and performance networks, encompassing guitar music, electronic pop and other self-directed approaches. Local scenes and international exchange have shaped diverse Russian-language and instrumental repertoires.

extras.description: Melodic vocals, interlocking guitars, bass and drums often support compact songs and contrasting textures. Synthesizers and electronic production open additional directions, ranging from restrained intimacy to forceful rhythmic interplay.

tradition.lineage: Russian plugg — a Russian-language branch of the airy, minimalist trap sound developed through online producer and rapper networks.

tradition.name: Russian rave
tradition.lineage: Russian rave is a Russian-language electronic scene connecting hard dance energy with pop melodies, rap-inflected delivery and youth-club culture. Artists such as GSPD, DEAD BLONDE and Lida span harder rave tracks and melodic synth-pop, bringing the music into both club and concert settings.

tradition.name: Spanish new wave
tradition.lineage: Spanish new wave emerged around the transition from the 1970s to the 1980s, connecting punk, pop and electronic influences with new independent scenes and La Movida. Alaska y Los Pegamoides and other formative groups helped establish a style later renewed by bands such as Juanita y Los Feos.

extras.description: Direct melodic songs, brisk rhythms, electric guitars, bass, drums and keyboard colours link punk energy with pop hooks. Synth-driven and guitar-led approaches coexist across the field.
exemplars: Juanita y Los Feos — Nueva Numancia (2014), complete12 songs

tradition.lineage: Brazilian television singing competitions connect regional performers with national audiences, broadcast bands and commercial recordings. Programmes such as The Voice Brasil draw on Brazilian song, pop, rock and international repertoire, emphasizing vocal interpretation and the transition from televised performances to concert careers.

extras.description: Prominent singing leads a flexible pop-band accompaniment of guitar, bass, drums and keyboards. Clear harmonic support and responsive instrumental accents leave room for phrasing, sustained notes, dynamic contrasts and memorable refrains.

tradition.name: Telugu indie
tradition.lineage: Telugu indie connects independent Telugu artists through self-authored releases, online circulation, collaboration and local live venues.

extras.description: Song-led bands combine shared vocals with guitar, bass, drums and keyboards, while the wider community also embraces rap and other styles. ChowRaasta exemplifies a folk- and reggae-inflected amplified branch alongside independent songwriters and MCs.

entries.geo_rationale: Firsthand source documents Hyderabad pub/college practice; editorial community anchor, not a claimed recording location.
entries.neighbor_distinction: Telugu indie denotes the cross-style independent Telugu music-making and circulation community. The Pioneer interviews the musicians themselves about self-authored releases, YouTube, mutual promotion and collaborations: ChowRaasta folk/reggae band, Roll Rida rap and Hemachandra independent songwriting all participate. This is a positive community field rather than a synonym for one band or its selected song. Existing telugu_folk already includes contemporary Chowraasta folk/reggae fusion; that overlap is explicit and is not excluded by date, modern instrumentation or independent release. Existing telugu_hip_hop likewise includes independent Roll Rida; the broader independently documented community crosses both folk and rap practices and includes other songwriters. Existing tollywood denotes Telugu cinema playback repertoire; musicians cross between film and independent work, so no personnel exclusion is claimed. The new field is distinguished by the documented independent production/collaboration network, not a different timbre or exemplar alone. No exact EveryNoise membership claimed because its map is inaccessible.

tradition.name: Vintage Italian Soundtrack
tradition.lineage: Vintage Italian soundtrack music draws on the film and studio archives of the 1960s–80s, where jazz, orchestral writing, pop, funk and psychedelic textures served comedy, crime, horror and other screen genres. Reissue and licensing communities around CAM Sugar and Sonor Music Editions have renewed circulation of this repertoire. Alongside orchestral scores, studio groups such as I Marc 4 supplied compact, groove-led themes built from guitar, organ, bass and drums.

extras.description: Short thematic cues move between memorable melody, rhythmic accompaniment and contrasting instrumental colours. Electric organ, guitar and a bass-and-drum rhythm section support the jazz-funk studio-combo strand, while the wider archival field also includes orchestral, electronic and vocal film music.

entries.geo_rationale: CAM founded Rome1960; representative historical studio and archive centre, not a claim about every source recording.
entries.model_policy: Genre-level representative jazz-funk studio-combo strand positively documented by its current publisher, not a reconstructed album or claim that all Italian scores use four instruments. Conventional single-coil electric guitar, passive electric bass, maple drumkit and B3/Leslie with mellow jazz registration, short percussion and slow rotary are authored practical realizations. No precise personal gear attribution. Broad field remains stylistically varied; the chosen default emphasizes repeating rhythm-section grooves, hence funk-percussion parent for this branch rather than genre-wide formal classification. All applicable controls retained. The selected treatment is a lively, pointed jazz-funk groove with a lighter organ response; it is not a claim that every archive cue shares that affect.

tradition.name: Violão Clássico
tradition.lineage: Brazilian concert-guitar practice connecting conservatory training, solo recitals and chamber performance with an international classical repertoire.

extras.description: Nylon-string guitar combines melody, bass and inner voices through fingerstyle articulation. Scales, arpeggios, chordal textures and contrasting tone colours support works and transcriptions from different periods. Brazilian performers and composers participate in a wider international concert and teaching tradition.

entries.geo_rationale: Editorial documented USP/RadioCultura concert-community anchor, not actual session venue or instrument birthplace.
entries.source_scope_limitation: Fabio Zanon — complete Guitar Recital, Naxos8.554431, all16 indexed tracks64:40, issued August1998. Label lists Zanon as sole artist and instrumental guitar recital, with Tarrega miniatures, all four Bach BWV1003 movements in his transcription, Alexandre de Faria, Mertz and Ponce. Artist discography identifies Sergio Abreu1986 guitar for this exact recital. One guitar performer, no voice or other ensemble inferred. This is the complete album, not a convenient excerpt from a larger orchestral recording; no audio audition claimed.
entries.neighbor_distinction: The requested creator ViolaoClassico field concentrates the Brazilian concert-guitar performer/composer network: Zanon, TuribioSantos, Abreu, Assad and their international repertoire circulation. It includes non-Brazilian interpreters of Brazilian compositions and European works, so neither exclusive citizenship nor exclusively Brazilian compositions is asserted. Zanon institutional biography documents USP training, Brazilian young-soloist/concert awards and the Brazilian Art/Music Bunge prize; his own biography documents RadioCultura concert-guitar broadcasting and CamposdoJordao festival leadership alongside international concert work. These provide a positive national concert-institution community, not Portuguese translation alone. Existing classical_guitar is the broad international concert instrument field, not restricted to its Shibe/Bach example. Existing violao_brasileiro already straddles concert and popular practice and includes VillaLobos, but its actual declared defining axis is choro-derived baixaria, syncopation and independent-thumb Brazilian instrumental language. The Brazilian concert-institution network overlaps that field while including European and international concert repertoire without requiring that rhythmic vocabulary. No strict disjointness or sonic novelty is claimed; this narrower community interpretation remains subject to independent category review. UNIRIO’s own institutional history independently distinguishes a ViolaoClassico teaching lineage beginning with TuribioSantos in1981 and continuing through NicolasdeSouzaBarros, MariaHaro and ClaytonVetromilla, alongside a separately identified ViolaoPopular lineage. Its faculty account follows concert-guitar graduates into federal and state teaching posts. This supplies a positively documented Brazilian conservatory network beyond the selected performer nationality; the anniversary archival study locates its concert/pedagogic formation historically while correcting older myths of exclusive elite origins. The requested creator field overlaps popular players and international interpreters, so the institutional network is a central concentration rather than an exhaustive membership rule.

tradition.name: Volkstümliche Musik
tradition.lineage: Volkstümliche Musik is a popular entertainment field drawing on folk-song models, regional imagery, marches and Schlager. Radio, television, film and touring performers helped develop its familiar melodies and public sing-along repertoire during the twentieth century.

extras.description: Clear vocal melodies, regular dance rhythms and approachable harmonies support songs of home, affection and sociability. Acoustic instruments and modern accompaniment coexist, with fluid connections to Alpine folk music and German-language Schlager.
exemplars: Gerhard Hildner — complete Musikantentreff130-title songbook MVH1000414

entries.geo_rationale: Approximate German-language repertoire land anchor; transnational German-speaking field not restricted to Germany, and no source recording location asserted.

Publisher specifies one melodic line, chord symbols and text, with tempo/rhythm indications; the catalogue labels a melody instrument in C and mentions keyboard, guitar and vocal accompaniment as uses. This is a lead-sheet publication, not three separately notated mandatory ensemble parts. The complete book is realized here through one singing lead and piano chordal accompaniment, preserving all published melody, harmony and text. This is explicitly an authored realization of the lead sheets, not a publisher-issued fully notated piano arrangement, an inspected score transcription, or a reconstruction of the original artists recordings. The publisher does not expressly say keyboard OR guitar, and that wording is not invented. No actual positively credited performance personnel are omitted: the earlier simultaneous three-family model was an editorial interpretation of possible uses, not a documented session roster. All 130 titles remain the scope. Authored functional-harmonic verse–chorus–bridge popular-song treatment follows the positive melody/chord/lyric publication; it does not assert identical form or tempo for every title. One natural singing lead and a standard-size modern upright piano with block-chord popular accompaniment are editorial performance choices. Brisk representative vocal pacing, piano construction and chordal gesture are not measured original tempo, publisher hardware or personal playing lineage. No universal temperament or recording apparatus is asserted. Controlled live-room presentation is authored.

tradition.name: German Dark Minimal Techno
tradition.lineage: German dark minimal techno developed through a 2010s independent-label network including Klangrecords, Darker Sounds, Subwoofer and Toxic Recordings, linking hard-minimal producers such as Timao with the darker industrial sound of Klangtronik.

extras.description: Heavy bass, stark repeating figures and abrasive electronic textures drive club-focused DJ sets and productions. Restrained motifs and sustained rhythmic pressure connect the style to minimal techno, while rougher textures and weightier impacts connect it to hard and industrial techno.

tradition.name: Malaysian Tamil Rap
tradition.lineage: Malaysian Tamil rap grew through local recording crews and producers such as Yogi B and Natchatra, connecting Malaysia’s multilingual hip-hop scene with Tamil-speaking audiences abroad.

extras.description: Tamil verses and rhythmic flows ride produced hip-hop accompaniment, ranging from personal and social commentary to celebratory tracks. tradition.name: Samba Moderno
tradition.lineage: Samba moderno follows the contemporary Rio singer-composer network nurtured by Lapa venues, Clube Renascença, Cacique de Ramos and projects such as Samba Social Clube and Festa da Raça. Artists including João Martins, Inácio Rios and Nego Álvaro carry older samba traditions into new compositions, collaborations and independent careers.

extras.description: Melodic singing and shared refrains interlock with compact cavaquinho or banjo accompaniment, guitar and layered hand percussion. New songs about affection, everyday life and social experience circulate between neighborhood rodas, studio releases and concert stages, retaining the rhythmic conversation of samba while developing individual poetic voices.

entries.geo_rationale: Primary interviews and broadcaster locate the named contemporary network in Rio neighborhoods and roda institutions.
entries.model_policy: Representative small-roda genre practice, not reconstruction of any named album or broadcast ensemble. Rhythmic syllabic group singing, Brazilian steel-string mahogany cavaquinho, medium goatskin pandeiro with wooden frame/brass jingles, and wooden tantã in pagode groove are practical authored choices within directly documented singing, cavaquinho/banjo and percussion practice. Guitar and other arrangements remain part of the wider field; the selected compact rendition does not claim an exhaustive fixed orchestration or exact historical gear. A lively, brisk percussion-led rendition and rhythmic vocal articulation are authored within the dance-oriented practice, not measured source-session acoustics or a universal tempo.

tradition.name: Indian Underground Rap
tradition.lineage: Indian underground rap developed through local crews, street cyphers, independent releases and online exchanges across cities and languages. Projects such as Hip Hop Homeland brought Mumbai, Kashmir, Punjab, Kolkata, Shillong and other communities into a shared public conversation, while neighborhood identity and everyday experience remained central.

extras.description: Rhythmic, text-forward verses work over producer-built beats or circulate through freestyle and battle settings. Local-language phrasing, code-switching, personal testimony and social criticism connect performers to their communities. Beat production ranges across boom-bap, trap and other hip-hop approaches rather than following one compulsory national rhythm.

tradition.name: Bouzouki
tradition.lineage: Bouzouki repertoire connects Greek instrumental performance, dance music and song adaptation with generations of players, composers and teachers. Recordings and published instrumental collections carry this practice beyond its rebetiko and laïkó roots into concert and international settings.

extras.description: Bright picked melodies, ringing paired strings and ornamented phrases lead the music. Free introductory taximia coexist with shaped dance tunes and instrumental versions of songs. Solo playing, small ensembles and larger arrangements provide different settings for the bouzouki’s melodic voice.

entries.geo_rationale: Greek instrumental repertoire institutional hub, not precise recording location; linked Athens/Piraeus urban song histories and contemporary national performer/teacher networks.

sources.support_notes: Fresh exact creator13763/13764:100 tracks, strongly Greek instrumental repertoire with taximia, dance forms, song transcriptions; Pappos8/55, Zambetas1/10/48. Irish player Alec Finn crossover at43 means not absolute geographic exclusivity.

Fresh artist-owned13767view0: instrumental compositions for three-string bouzouki,48 score collections including bouzouki instrumentals and curriculum, ensemble extending Greek/Mediterranean songs. Supports repertoire/community, not exact master closure.

Fresh issuer13757view1: instrumental bouzouki-led dances across Greek regions and Greek-American circulation; not an assertion all listed ensemble roles are known or required.

entries.neighbor_distinction: Full Rebetiko is an urban vocal-song/history category; full Laiko is postwar popular song and expanded band arrangement. Both already feature ornamental bouzouki and overlap this field. The creator instrument-centered repertoire and artist-owned instrumental curriculum/collections positively include solo taximia, dance instrumentals and transcriptions spanning those traditions; this is a repertoire field rather than a synonym for one vocal genre or simply a claim about player nationality. Full Greek Folk contains many regional instrument traditions beyond bouzouki. Irish bouzouki is a different adaptation with some crossover participants; Greek-led repertoire is the representative branch here.
entries.model_policy: Representative solo melodic instrumental practice, supported by bouzouki instrumental curriculum and taxim repertoire. Three-course Greek bouzouki, walnut bowl, paired modern steel strings and medium plectrum with ornamented melodic picking are explicit authored settings, not a claim about one player’s precise instrument or a complete released master. No singer required for this instrumental branch; song accompaniment and larger ensembles remain part of the public field. Controlled live room is editable contemporary capture. Broader improvisation frame reflects melodic taxim realization without declaring all repertoire free improvisation. All five meaningful construction/performance controls retained.

tradition.lineage: Chilean drill developed within the country’s rap and urban-music networks as artists adapted an international hip-hop style to local voices and stories. Musicians move between drill, trap and other approaches, with independent beatmakers and online releases connecting the scene.

extras.description: Rapped phrases work against producer-built drill beats, giving rhythm, delivery and personal narrative a central role. Chilean vocabulary and local experience shape the verses, while collaborative studio production links performers to a wider urban scene.

tradition.name: Indonesian Emo Rap
tradition.lineage: Indonesian emo rap joins the country’s hip-hop communities with the emotional themes and expressive textures of emo. Independent rappers and producers use personal recollection, alienation and regret alongside social criticism, with artists such as Anjar OX’S and Walkingpasttheex representing different approaches.

extras.description: Confessional verses and melodic passages meet producer-shaped hip-hop and trap accompaniment. The emphasis falls on emotional directness and atmosphere, while performers move between rapped and sung delivery and draw on rock-related or electronic textures.

tradition.name: Medimeisterschaften
tradition.lineage: Medimeisterschaften music grew from the themed songs and fan culture of European medical-student gatherings. University teams write, produce and perform their own annual tracks, tying local identity and playful slogans to costumes, videos and collective festival participation.

extras.description: Catchy sung lines, rhythmic slogans and produced beats carry university-specific wordplay and shared refrains. Student teams build melody, harmony and rhythm together, record and edit vocals, and bring the songs from bedroom studios to festival stages. Styles vary with each year’s theme and contributors.

tradition.name: Tamaulipas Rap
tradition.lineage: Tamaulipas rap connects local MCs, independent crews, beatmakers and event networks across the northeastern Mexican state. Regional interviews document both shared scene-building and disagreement over its direction, while artists carry local experiences into wider Mexican rap circuits.

extras.description: Text-forward rhythmic verses ride producer-built beats. Personal experience, regional identity, protest and everyday life supply varied lyrical material, with independent recording and live events sustaining the community. Production approaches differ across artists rather than following a single compulsory regional instrument set.

tradition.name: Indie campechano
tradition.lineage: Campeche’s independent music scene grew through local bands, self-organized concerts and regional recording networks. MOROCA connected underground rock musicians in the 2000s; La Caverna and Indie Fest Campeche later linked this history with new pop, alternative and electronic projects. Studios and community radio supported releases, while Ciudad del Carmen developed its own artist-organized concert activity.

extras.description: Guitar-led songs, bass lines, drum-kit grooves and sung melodies form a common band foundation, with keyboards adding harmonic layers and electronic colors. The scene encompasses melodic pop, danceable funk and synth textures as well as heavier rock and metal. Independent production and regional collaboration connect these varied sounds.

entries.geo_rationale: Regional scene anchor in Campeche; Ciudad del Carmen and other state communities remain included.

tradition.name: Malawian hip hop
tradition.lineage: Malawian hip hop developed through local rappers, independent producers, labels and collaborations linking urban communities with wider African audiences. Artists such as Biriwiri, Dizzo and Macelba helped establish vernacular rap and studio-made beats alongside English-language and cross-border work. Chichewa expression, local experience and connections with older popular traditions remain important parts of the scene.

extras.description: Rhythmic verses sit over producer-built beats, with memorable sung hooks and switches between rapping and singing in some branches. Lyrics move between everyday experience, personal confidence and social reflection. Production varies by artist and producer, from direct hip-hop grooves to arrangements incorporating local melodic and rhythmic references.

tradition.name: Fan chant
tradition.lineage: Fan chants are participatory repertoires of sports supporters, transmitted through matches, supporter groups and recordings. Football terraces are a major setting, alongside cricket, basketball and baseball crowds. Team names, player songs and adapted familiar melodies turn local allegiance into collective sound; leaders and neighboring groups can cue new chants or bring them back after interruptions.

extras.description: Short repeated phrases, syllabic delivery and collective rhythmic entry make fan chants easy to join. Pitched motifs and recited slogans coexist, with clapping and drums reinforcing the pulse in organized supporter groups. Repetition, call-and-response cues and changing crowd intensity sustain the chant rather than elaborate harmonic development.

Bandola/tiple rhythmic strumming with lyrical pasillo lead context and guitar free-stroke fingerpicking are deliberately arranged gestures, not source-measured technique. Spruce-top/fan-braced normal-tension nylon guitar and cedar steel-course tiple are ordinary authored construction. Broad artMusic scopes the composed concert-trio practice positively documented by the venue, not a universal claim all folk music serves concert listening. Authored recital hall and responsive spruce-top nylon guitar support clear ensemble projection and dynamic contrast in this positively documented concert-trio practice, without asserting the original venue geometry or source guitar materials.

tradition.name: Chhattisgarhi pop
tradition.lineage: Chhattisgarhi pop links regional-language songwriting and modern folk with a local album, film and concert industry. Singers such as Nitin Dubey developed audiences through recordings and stage performances before artist channels and music videos widened circulation. Folk melody, playback singing and studio production remain connected within this regional field.

Electronic rhythm, programmed sounds and effects support contemporary songs, while other arrangements incorporate folk instruments and film-music textures. Repeated hooks and direct vocal phrasing connect recorded songs with stage audiences.
